metric: share of reef area hit by bleaching-level heat
statement: The largest global bleaching event on record (previous: 68% in 2014–2017).

metric: warm-water coral reefs: further decline
statement: A further decline of 70–90% at 1.5 °C, more than 99% at 2 °C.

metric: displacement
statement: Weather and climate extremes are increasingly driving people from their homes in all regions, with small island states disproportionately affected.

metric: people living in internal displacement after disasters
statement: On 31 December 2025 almost 13.6 million people were still living away from home inside their own country because of a disaster; people who fled abroad are not included. Disasters here include earthquakes and volcanoes as well as weather. During 2025, disasters caused 29.9 million displacements: that counts every move, so one person can count more than once, and some moves are temporary or pre-emptive, such as evacuations before a storm.

farm productivity growth
statement: Farm productivity has grown, but climate change has slowed that growth globally (medium confidence), mainly in mid and low latitudes; some high-latitude regions gained.

metric: global agricultural total factor productivity lost to climate change
statement: One study puts the loss at about 21% since 1961, compared with a world without human-caused climate change: as if the last 7 years of growth had been lost. Warmer regions such as Africa and Latin America lost about 26 to 34%. The study's uncertainty range is wide.

metric: glacier ice lost per year
statement: Since 2000 about 5% of glacier ice has gone; yearly loss was about 36% higher in 2012–2023 than in 2000–2011.

statement: In 732 places in 43 countries; the share ranges from 20.5% to 76.3% from country to country.

metric: Greenland and Antarctic ice lost
statement: Enough to raise sea level by 21 mm; the yearly loss more than tripled.

metric: surface ocean pH
statement: As the ocean takes up CO₂ it turns more acidic: surface open-ocean pH as low as in recent decades is unusual in the last 2 million years (medium confidence).

metric: open-ocean surface pH decline per decade
statement: Open-ocean surface pH has fallen by 0.017 to 0.027 units per decade since the late 1980s (very likely range, from measurement records longer than 15 years); over more than 95% of the ocean surface the decline already stands out from natural variation.

metric: 2021 Pacific Northwest heatwave: times less likely without climate change
statement: About 2 °C hotter than it would have been in 1850–1900, and still a rare event in today's climate (about once in 1,000 years by the study's estimate).
